Tensor Analysis – Practical 4 Solutions Information: • Please make sure to complete all exercises before the next lecture. • The exercises marked with [See lecture] were solved in class. • The exercises are not organised by difficulty. 4.1 Given an orthogonal coordinate system K with orthonormal basis i1, i2, i3, consider the a new coordinate system K′ with basis vectors e1 = i1 + i2 − i3, e2 = i1 + i2, e3 = i1 − i3. (1) Find a basis e1, e2, e3 dual to e1, e2, e3. (2) Find the covariant components of the vector joining the origin to the point (2, 0, −1). (3) Find the contravariant components of the vector joining the origin to the point (2, 0, −1). Solution: (1) We have e1 =   1 1 −1   , e2 =   1 1 0   , e3 =   1 0 −1   . We will need e1 × e2 =   1 1 −1   ×   1 1 0   =   1 −1 0   e2 × e3 =   1 1 0   ×   1 0 −1   =   −1 1 −1   e3 × e1 =   1 0 −1   ×   1 1 −1   =   1 0 1   . We still need to compute V : V = e1 · (e2 × e3) =   1 1 −1   ·  −1 1 −1   = 1. 1

# Page 2^page=2
2 Applying to the dual basis formula, we get e 1 = e2 × e3 e1 · (e2 × e3) =  −1 1 −1   e 2 = e3 × e1 e2 · (e3 × e1) =  1 0 1   e 3 = e1 × e2 e3 · (e1 × e2) =   1 −1 0   . Remark: When computing V , we can pick any of the three formulas: V = e1 · (e2 × e3) =   1 1 −1   ·  −1 1 −1   = 1, V = e2 · (e3 × e1) =  1 1 0   ·  1 0 1   = 1, V = e3 · (e1 × e2) =   1 0 −1   ·   1 −1 0   = 1. (2) Let A = 2i1 − i3. The covariant components of the vector A with respect to K′ are the coefficients of the expansion A = A1e 1 + A2e 2 + A3e 3. You can solve the system to find A1, A2, A3, or you can use the formula Ai = A · ei. Let us show the second method: A1 = A · e1 =   1 0 −1   ·   1 1 −1   = 2, A2 = A · e2 =   1 0 −1   ·  1 1 0   = 1, A3 = A · e3 =   1 0 −1   ·   1 0 −1   = 2.

# Page 3^page=3
3 (3) Let A = 2i1 − i3 again. The contravariant components of the vector A with respect to K′ are the coefficients of the expansion A = A1e1 + A2e2 + A3e3. Again, you can either solve the system above to find A1, A2, A3, or you can use the formula Ai = A · ei. We use the easier method: A1 = A · e 1 =   1 0 −1   ·   −1 1 −1   = 0, A2 = A · e 2 =   1 0 −1   ·   1 0 1   = 0, A3 = A · e 3 =   1 0 −1   ·   1 −1 0   = 1. 4.2 [See lecture] Given an orthogonal coordinate system K with orthonormal basis i1, i2, i3, consider the a new coordinate system K′ with basis vectors e1 = i1 + 2i2 + 4i3, e2 = i2, e3 = i1 + 2i2 + 5i3. (1) Find a basis e1, e2, e3 dual to e1, e2, e3. (2) Find the covariant components of the vector joining the origin to the point (1, 1, 1). (3) Find the contravariant components of the vector joining the origin to the point (1, 1, 1). Solution: (1) Here, we have e1 =   1 2 4   , e2 =   0 1 0   , e3 =   1 2 5   .

# Page 4^page=4
4 We will need e1 × e2 =   1 2 4   ×   0 1 0   =   −4 0 1   e2 × e3 =   0 1 0   ×   1 2 5   =   5 0 −1   e3 × e1 =   1 2 5   ×   1 2 4   =   −2 1 0   . We still need to compute V : V = e2 · (e3 × e1) =   0 1 0   ·   −2 1 0   = 1. Applying to the dual basis formula, we get e 1 = e2 × e3 e1 · (e2 × e3) = e2 × e3 =   5 0 −1   e 2 = e3 × e1 e2 · (e3 × e1) = e3 × e1 =   −2 1 0   e 3 = e1 × e2 e3 · (e1 × e2) = e1 × e2 =   −4 0 1   . (2) Let B = i1 + i2 + i3. The covariant components of the vector B with respect to K′ are the coefficients of the expansion B = B1e 1 + B2e 2 + B3e 3. They are given by the formula Bi = B · ei:

# Page 5^page=5
5 B1 = B · e1 =  1 1 1   ·   1 2 4   = 7, B2 = B · e2 =  1 1 1   ·   0 1 0   = 1, B3 = B · e3 =   1 1 1   ·   1 2 5   = 8. (3) Let B = i1 + i2 + i3. The contravariant components of the vector B with respect to K′ are the coefficients of the expansion B = B1e1 + B2e2 + B3e3, which are given by the formula Ai = A · ei: B1 = B · e 1 =  1 1 1   ·   5 0 −1   = 4, B2 = B · e 2 =  1 1 1   ·   −2 1 0   = −1, B3 = B · e 3 =  1 1 1   ·   −4 0 1   = −3. 4.3 Given an orthogonal coordinate system K with orthonormal basis i1, i2, i3, consider the a new coordinate system K′ with basis vectors e1 = i1 + 2i2, e2 = 2i1 + 2i2 + 4i3, e3 = 2i3. (1) Find a basis e1, e2, e3 dual to e1, e2, e3. (2) Find the covariant components of the vector C = 2i2 + 2i3. (3) Find the contravariant components of the vector C = 2i2 + 2i3.

# Page 6^page=6
6 Solution: (1) Here, we have e1 =   1 2 0   , e2 =   2 2 4   , e3 =   0 0 2   . We will need e1 × e2 =   1 2 0   ×   2 2 4   =   8 −4 −2   e2 × e3 =   2 2 4   ×   0 0 2   =   4 −4 0   e3 × e1 =   0 0 2   ×   1 2 0   =   −4 2 0   . We also need: V = e3 · (e1 × e2) =  0 0 2   ·   8 −4 −2   = −4. Applying to the dual basis formula, we get e 1 = e2 × e3 e1 · (e2 × e3) = e2 × e3 −4 =   −1 1 0   e 2 = e3 × e1 e2 · (e3 × e1) = e3 × e1 −4 =   1 − 1 2 0   e 3 = e1 × e2 e3 · (e1 × e2) = e1 × e2 −4 =   −2 1 1 2   . (2) The covariant components of the vector C with respect to K′ are the coefficients of the expansion C = C1e 1 + C2e 2 + C3e 3. They are given by the formula Ci = C · ei:

# Page 7^page=7
7 C1 = C · e1 =   0 2 2   ·   1 2 0   = 4, C2 = C · e2 =   0 2 2   ·   2 2 4   = 12, C3 = C · e3 =   0 2 2   ·   0 0 2   = 4. (3) The contravariant components of the vector C with respect to K′ are the coefficients of the expansion C = C1e1 + C2e2 + C3e3, which are given by the formula Ai = A · ei: C1 = C · e 1 =   0 2 2   ·  −1 1 0   = 2, C2 = C · e 2 =   0 2 2   ·   1 − 1 2 0   = −1, C3 = C · e 3 =   0 2 2   ·   −2 1 1 2   = 3. 4.4 Given an orthogonal coordinate system K with orthonormal basis i1, i2, i3, consider the vector B with components B = i1 + 3i2. Let K be a new coordinate system with basis vectors e ′ 1 = i1, e ′ 2 = i1 − i2, e ′ 3 = i1 + i2 + i3. (1) Work out the expansion coefficients L1 i′, L2 i′, L3 i′ for each i = 1, 2, 3. (2) Compute the covariant components B′ i of B in the coordinate system K′. (3) Find a basis dual to e′ 1, e′ 2, e′ 3. (4) Compute the contravariant components B′i of B in the coordinate system K′.

# Page 8^page=8
8 (5) Let gik = e′i ·e′k. Compute these gik for all i, k = 1, 2, 3. (It might be more convenient to write your answers as the entries of a matrix.) (6) Using your answers to parts (2) and (5), work out the contravariant components B′i of B in K′ in another way. Solution: (1) We Ln m′ = e′ m · in, so L 1 1′ = 1, L 2 1′ = 0, L 3 1′ = 0, L 1 2′ = 1, L 2 2′ = −1, L 3 2′ = 0, L 1 3′ = 1, L 2 3′ = 1, L 3 3′ = 1. (2) Hence, from B′ i = Lj i′Bj we obtain B′ 1 = L 1 1′B1 + L 2 1′B2 + L 3 1′B3 = 1, B′ 2 = L 1 2′B1 + L 2 2′B2 + L 3 2′B3 = −2, B′ 3 = L 1 3′B1 + L 2 3′B2 + L 3 3′B3 = 4. (3) We have e ′ 1 =   1 0 0   , e ′ 2 =   1 −1 0   , e ′ 3 =   1 1 1   . We will need e ′ 1 × e ′ 2 =   1 0 0   ×   1 −1 0   =   0 0 −1   e ′ 2 × e ′ 3 =   1 −1 0   ×   1 1 1   =   −1 −1 2   e ′ 3 × e ′ 1 =   1 1 1   ×   1 0 0   =   0 1 −1   . Now e ′1 = e′2 × e′3 e′1 · (e′2 × e′3) = −   −1 −1 2   =   1 1 −2   ,

# Page 9^page=9
9 e ′2 = e′3 × e′1 e′2 · (e′3 × e′1) = −   0 1 −1   =   0 −1 1   , e ′3 = e′1 × e′2 e′3 · (e′1 × e′2) = −   0 0 −1   =   0 0 1   , gives us the dual basis. (4) We have Lm′ n = e′m · in, thus L 1′ 1 = 1, L 1′ 2 = 1, L 1′ 3 = −2, L 2′ 1 = 0, L 2′ 2 = −1, L 2′ 3 = 1, L 3′ 1 = 0, L 3′ 2 = 0, L 3′ 3 = 1. Hence, from B′i = Li′ j Bj we obtain B′1 = L 1′ 1 B1 + L 1′ 2 B2 + L 1′ 3 B3 = 4, B′2 = L 2′ 1 B1 + L 2′ 2 B2 + L 2′ 3 B3 = −3, B′3 = L 3′ 1 B1 + L 3′ 2 B2 + L 3′ 3 B3 = 0. (5) It is easier to write gik as a matrix: gik =   6 −3 −2 −3 2 1 −2 1 1   . (6) We will use the relation B′i = gikB′ k = ∑3 k=1 gikB′ k. Performing this straightforward computation yields the same answers as in part (4). 4.5 [Question from Final Exam 23-24] In this question, denote by K the Cartesian coordinate system with vector basis i1, i2, i3, the standard orthonormal basis of R3. Denote by K′ the coordinate system with vector basis e1, e2, e3 given by e1 = 2i1 + i3 e2 = i2 e3 = i1 − i2 + i3. (1) Find the dual basis e1, e2, e3.

# Page 10^page=10
10 (2) Find the covariant and contravariant components of the vector V = 3i1 − 2i2 + i3 with respect to the bases e1, e2, e3 and e1, e2, e3. Solution: (a) We have e1 = ( 2 0 1 ) e2 = ( 0 1 0 ) e3 = ( 1 −1 1 ) . We will need e1 × e2 = ( 2 0 1 ) × ( 0 1 0 ) = ( −1 0 2 ) e2 × e3 = ( 0 1 0 ) × ( 1 −1 1 ) = ( 1 0 −1 ) e3 × e1 = ( 1 −1 1 ) × ( 2 0 1 ) = ( −1 1 2 ) . Notice that e1 · (e2 × e3) = e2 · (e3 × e1) = e3 · (e1 × e2) = 1. Consequently e 1 = e2 × e3 e1 · (e2 × e3) = e2 × e3 = ( 1 0 −1 ) e 2 = e3 × e1 e2 · (e3 × e1) = e3 × e1 = ( −1 1 2 ) e 3 = e1 × e2 e3 · (e1 × e2) = e1 × e2 = ( −1 0 2 ) . (b) The covariant components of V are given by Vi = V · ei. Thus V1 = ( 3 −2 1 ) · ( 2 0 1 ) = 7, V2 = ( 3 −2 1 ) · ( 0 1 0 ) = −2, V3 = ( 3 −2 1 ) · ( 1 −1 1 ) = 6. Similarly, the contravariant components of V are given by V i = V · e i. Thus V1 = ( 3 −2 1 ) · ( 1 0 −1 ) = 2, V2 = ( 3 −2 1 ) · ( −1 1 2 ) = −3, V3 = ( 3 −2 1 ) · ( −1 0 2 ) = −1.

# Page 11^page=11
11 4.6 Consider dual bases e1, e2, e3 and e1, e2, e3, and denote V = e1 · (e2 × e3), and V ′ = e 1 · (e 2 × e 3). Show, using the vector triple product formula, that V ′ = 1/V . Solution: In the lectures, we have shown V ′ = e 1 · (e2 × e3). As e 1 = e2 × e3 V , e 2 = e3 × e1 V , e 3 = e1 × e2 V , we have V ′ = e2 × e3 V · ( e3 × e1 V × e1 × e2 V ) = 1 V 3 (e2 × e3) · (((e3 × e1) · e2)e1 − ((e3 × e1) · e1)e2) = 1 V 3 (e2 × e3) · ((e3 × e1) · e2)e1) (because (e3 × e1) ⊥ e1) = 1 V 3 (e2 × e3) · (V e1) = 1 V 2 (e2 × e3) · e1 = 1 V , as required. 4.7 [See lecture] Express the scalar triple product (A × B) · C in terms of the covariant and contravariant components of the vectors A, B and C, with respect to dual bases. You may use the equalities (1) A × B = (AjBk − AkBj)V = 1 V (AjBk − AkBj). Solution: Writing D = A × B, we have from Example 3.8 that, D = Die i = (AjBk − AkBj)V e i = Diei = 1 V (AjBk − AkBj)ei. Thus, writing E = D · C, we obtain E = Diei · Cℓeℓ = giℓ V (AjBk − AkBj)Cℓ,

12 as giℓ = ei · eℓ. Similarly, E = Die i · Cℓe ℓ = giℓV (AjBk − AkBj)Cℓ, E = Diei · Cℓe ℓ = 1 V (AjBk − AkBj)Cℓ, and E = Die i · Cℓeℓ = V (AjBk − AkBj)Cℓ.
